source.title: Learning with Random Learning Rates
source.authors: Léonard Blier; Pierre Wolinski; Y. Ollivier

record.file_problem: Full text supplied; no apparent truncation or document mismatch.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports optimization and generalization performance of Alrao versus tuned SGD and default Adam, including train/test overfit observations. These experiments do not test the listed claim versions about memorization capacity, width beyond interpolation, convolutional inductive bias, optimizer generalization, batch size, dropout, sharpness, or memorized-example removal.
record.gate_note: The paper’s test-loss and validation results concern its proposed learning-rate method and optimizer comparisons, not the claim versions listed. Frozen-feature results concern training performance and are not reported as test-error comparisons. Cited results from other papers are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own Adam-versus-SGD held-out comparisons on image classification and character prediction, bearing on V4. Default Adam receives no tuning, whereas SGD's learning rate is selected by validation performance; this asymmetry limits the comparison but does not make it irrelevant. The record incorrectly excludes these results.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's main paraphrase is accurate: SGD-based Alrao reliably approaches the best tested fixed-rate SGD when its interval contains a suitable learning rate, whereas default Adam is less reliable. The authors additionally conclude that Adam sometimes overfits despite good training performance, directly connecting their findings to prior optimizer-generalization results.
record.recipe_differences: The study introduces Alrao, assigning random per-feature learning rates and averaging output classifiers; it evaluates image, language, and reinforcement-learning tasks rather than the listed generalization interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Alrao performance depends on the learning-rate interval containing a suitable rate; Adam shows setup-dependent optimization failures and overfitting. Combining Alrao with Adam produced unstable or diverging test performance in reported CIFAR10 experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: Default Adam fails to begin optimizing AlexNet on ImageNet: test accuracy is 0.10%, versus 53.2% for tuned SGD.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Default optimizer settings can fail to optimize particular architectures; this result does not isolate a generalization disadvantage after successful fitting.

fits_no_version.finding: Alrao generally approaches tuned SGD's performance; Alrao-Adam can overfit severely despite successful optimization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Random per-feature learning rates with output-model averaging can train reliably with SGD, while combining this recipe with Adam can destabilize held-out performance.

fits_no_version.finding: GoogLeNet retains useful CIFAR10 test performance when only a random fraction of features is trained.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Image classifiers can tolerate leaving some randomly selected features at initialization.

record.code_released: not stated; the text says a PyTorch implementation is released alongside the paper, but supplies no URL.
record.problems: ImageNet experiments are single runs. The paper's claim-relevant generalization observations are primarily optimizer comparisons, not tests of the cataloged versions; some supplementary learning-curve results are figure-only.
record.rows_left_out: No rows meet the version-specific row criteria. The paper’s optimizer performance table and train/test learning curves concern Alrao and default Adam, not any tested version. Figure 8 reports test loss against the fraction of trained features, but does not compare training and test error or test the named version claims.

untested.parts: No width sweep establishing interpolation or continued improvement beyond zero training error.
No equally tuned Adam-versus-SGD comparison, learning-rate schedules, broader hyperparameter tuning, decoupled weight decay, optimizer switching, or word-level language modeling.
No removal of examples selected by memorization.

missing.what: Restore the direct default-Adam versus tuned-SGD comparisons for the six standard-width image models and the PTB LSTM, recording test loss and accuracy separately. The record explicitly omits these comparisons, but its reason for excluding them from V4 is incorrect.
missing.locator: Table 1; Section 5 for validation selection, tuning asymmetry, and replication counts.

missing.what: Record the explicitly reported MobileNet overfitting despite good training performance and the later overfitting of standard-width ImageNet ResNet50 and DenseNet121. Keep checkpoint results separate from subsequent training trajectories.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for V4. All verdicts rely on the supplied text because the record has no rows. ImageNet results are single runs; CIFAR10 Table 1 results use ten runs and PTB five. Tripled-width Adam results lack matched tuned-SGD baselines. Figures contain inconsistent architecture captions, so attribution above follows Section 6 and panel labels.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not compare fitting fixed random labels with generalization on natural labels.
Width is increased threefold for Alrao and Adam in selected comparisons, but the study does not sweep width across the interpolation threshold or report the claim’s zero-training-error relation.
The study uses convolutional architectures but has no fully connected image-model comparator testing convolutional inductive bias.
Adam is compared with SGD and Alrao, but the study does not test adaptive-versus-SGD generalization under the conditions in this version.
The study does not vary batch size or test a large-batch generalization gap.
Dropout appears in the Penn Treebank LSTM setup, but dropout is not varied or evaluated as an intervention.
The study does not measure sharpness or compare generalization-gap measures.
The study does not identify or remove memorized training examples.

relationships.condition: Default Adam versus validation-selected fixed-rate SGD: CIFAR10 MobileNet and VGG19, ImageNet DenseNet121, and character-level Penn Treebank LSTM.
relationships.reason: From Table 1, absent from the empty record: Adam versus SGD accuracy is 78 versus 90.2%, 88.9 versus 89.5%, 67.9 versus 69.7%, and 65.6 versus 66.1%, respectively; Adam also has higher loss in each comparison. Section 6 explicitly attributes MobileNet's deficit to overfitting despite good training performance. Adam was not tuned.
relationships.display_finding: Reported accuracy and loss favored selected-rate SGD over untuned Adam, with MobileNet's deficit attributed to overfitting despite good training performance; these findings remain unverified.

relationships.condition: Default Adam versus validation-selected fixed-rate SGD: CIFAR10 GoogLeNet and ImageNet ResNet50 at standard width, using validation-selected checkpoints.
relationships.reason: From Table 1, absent from the record: GoogLeNet accuracy slightly favors Adam, 89.8 versus 89.6%, while loss favors SGD, 0.45 versus 0.47. ResNet50 accuracy is nearly equal, 67.1 versus 67.4%, while loss favors Adam, 1.39 versus 1.49. The optimizer ranking depends on the measure.
relationships.display_finding: Reported comparisons remain unverified and favor Adam or SGD differently depending on architecture, accuracy, and loss.

relationships.condition: ImageNet standard-width ResNet50 and DenseNet121 during continued training after good validation performance.
relationships.reason: Section 6 and Figures 2a and 5b explicitly report subsequent Adam overfitting; this text-based verdict concerns training trajectories, distinct from Table 1's selected checkpoints. No rows capture the finding.
relationships.display_finding: Adam reportedly overfit during continued training after achieving good validation performance, but these trajectory comparisons remain unverified.
